note: The OLG covers the dual participation requirement well: the 'TBA - Reporting Requirements During Case Maintenance' page states that 'The Department will adjust a TBA household's benefits and pay the new amount only when a TBA household member applies for SNAP benefits in a separate household or joins another active SNAP household.' It also correctly states that TBA households are not required to report or verify any changes during the 5-month TBA period. However, two FNS requirements are not adequately addressed: (1) The household's right to be recertified at any time during the transitional period is not explicitly stated. The OLG lists 'client's request' as a closing reason during TBA but does not frame this as a recertification option that ends transitional benefits and transitions to standard review procedures. (2) The FNS state option to act on changes reported by another program in which the household participates is not addressed at all — the OLG only identifies dual participation as the circumstance triggering TBA benefit adjustment, omitting the inter-program change reporting option. Whether Massachusetts has opted into this state option is not documented in the OLG.
